ultimasNoticias.entradilla: With a turnout of 87.33%, 76.76% of the votes cast backed the agreement; 20.26% rejected it and 2.98% were abstentions. 13,560 people voted, in person and online, on 30 September and 1 October.
ultimasNoticias.desconvocatoria: On 5 October, the Strike Committee — made up of CGT, ÚTIL and UGT — formally called off the indefinite strike, after the workforce backed the agreement by a large majority.

texto: The referendum closes the negotiation, but not the legal process. The battle over the industrial legitimacy of the agreement has all but been decided in Airbus's favour; the legal question is a very different one, and it remains open: whether the fundamental right to strike was violated during the process, and whether the company bargained in bad faith.
That is what Spain's National High Court (Audiencia Nacional) hears on 4 November 2026, at the hearing on the substance of CGT's claim. That is where all the attention now lies.

puntos.texto: Real CPI plus 2 points in January 2026 and 2027 and in April 2028, and plus 1.95 in April 2029: that is how 7.95% of lost purchasing power is recovered over four years. On top of that, every year, a 0.5% individual pay review and another 0.5% for promotions.
€2,000 gross, non-consolidated, in October 2026, to make up for the 'April effect' for everyone employed on the date the agreement is validated.

The current remote-work policy stays and individual agreements are respected, including those for 40% remote work and those for two days a week. Holidays: two mandatory weeks and two flexible ones (previously three and one). Those without free canteen access will pay €3.50 instead of €5 from 1 October.

Before 1 November, a committee will review workloads at Cádiz. A working group opens to negotiate a new absenteeism control system — the company withdraws its appeal to the Supreme Court — and talks on pay policy (PG-121) will begin before the end of 2026.

conflicto.title: How the current dispute came about.
conflicto.intro: The mobilisation of the Airbus Spain workforce —a first strike from 1 to 24 July 2026 and a second strike from 24 August to 5 October— arises, according to the movement’s manifesto, from a gradual deterioration of trust and accumulated disagreements over pay negotiations and working conditions. It also comes at a time of economic strength for the company. These are the demands the movement puts forward:

docManifiesto.grupo: Manifesto to the Airbus Group – July 2026

points.d: Inflation (CPI) as the basis for pay reviews from 2026, plus an extraordinary rise to offset the accumulated loss.
points.detalle: The economic dossier drawn up by the movement estimates an accumulated loss of purchasing power over recent years.
exige: Restoring CPI as the basis for annual pay reviews (RSG) from 2026.
An extraordinary increase, separate from the annual review, to compensate for the purchasing power lost over recent years.

points.d: Remote work at the worker's choice where the role allows, and flexibility in managing holidays.
points.detalle: Work-life balance cannot be treated as a privilege: it is a modern organisational tool that supports productivity, commitment and people’s wellbeing. Airbus has been a benchmark here for years. The movement considers that recent decisions represent a step backwards compared with the previous model.
exige: The option, at the worker's choice and in roles whose nature allows it, of working 40% of the week remotely, with compensatory measures for roles requiring greater on-site presence.
Restoring flexibility in holiday management, letting teams organise it among themselves while keeping two weeks in August as a recommendation.

points.d: A universal, free canteen with no co-payments or payroll deductions; maintaining the transport routes.
points.detalle: The movement calls for changes to these services to be subject to negotiation.
exige: A guaranteed universal, free canteen for Airbus workers, with no co-payments or payroll deductions.
Maintaining the current level of the transport route service.

points.d: Health must not be treated as a productivity metric: remove the factor or exclude medical leave from it.
points.detalle: The movement maintains that health protection must take precedence in the organisation of work.
exige: Removal of the Bradford factor or, failing that, exclusion of medical leave from its calculation.

points.t: Protecting the future of Airbus Spain
points.d: Written guarantees that organisational changes will not harm jobs or working conditions.
points.detalle: The manifesto calls for organisational transformations to be subject to negotiation and to include guarantees for the workforce.
exige: Management signing the schedule of guarantees backed by a majority of the Space workforce, committing in writing that its implementation will not harm working conditions, work organisation or employment.

points.d: A transparent pay policy recognising experience and responsibility, with no gaps based on joining date.
points.detalle: The pay and benefits model must recognise every worker's contribution and experience, and guarantee equal opportunity, avoiding differences arising solely from the date they joined the company.
exige: A signed commitment to draw up a new pay policy with a transparent system for recognising experience, duties performed and responsibility held.
Ending prolonged entry-level pay, guaranteeing pay progression in line with the worker's real contribution.

points.d: An extraordinary, individual compensation, proportional to the strike days observed.
exige: Establishing an extraordinary, individual compensation for each worker, proportional to the strike days actually observed.

horquilla.label: BREAKING POINT · ESTIMATED IMPACT ON THE COMPANY
horquilla.intro: It is not what Airbus reports losing: it is an outside estimate built on public facts — what each plant makes and its role in the supply chain — and on two scenarios.
horquilla.finLabel: Projection to the end of the window
horquilla.cotaMin: Lower bound: inventory holds for the whole window
horquilla.cotaMax: Upper bound: the chain breaks around week three
horquilla.nota: Scenario estimate from an independent tracker, built on public facts and on each plant's role in the supply chain. It is not an official Airbus figure nor a verified quantification of the dispute: it is an order of magnitude, refreshed daily from the source.
horquilla.ejeAria: Minimum–maximum cumulative band of the estimated impact, from

como.t: There are two regimes, not one
como.d: While plants draw on accumulated inventory, a day of stoppage costs little: assembly carries on with what was in the warehouse. That is the buffer regime. Once a plant runs that buffer down, final assembly lines run out of parts and the daily cost multiplies: that is the breakdown regime.

como.t: That is why the curve steepens
como.d: Day 1 does not cost what day 25 costs. A day of closure at Getafe costs half a million at the start; with stabilisers exhausted, between six and ten. Up to twelve times more for the same day of strike.

como.t: The band is two hypotheses, not an error margin
como.d: The lower line assumes inventory holds for the whole window without breaking. The upper line assumes it breaks around week three. What actually happens will sit somewhere between the two.

como.t: What to watch to know which way it is going
como.d: The most direct indicator is Beluga traffic, the aircraft that moves parts between factories. While it holds up, the company is compensating with inventory; a sustained drop is the sign that the chain has started to feel it.

horquilla.desactualizado: This analysis dates from {fecha} and does not yet take the second strike call into account. The band keeps growing on the assumptions of that date, so read it as an order of magnitude, not an up-to-date figure. This notice will disappear on its own as soon as the source refreshes the analysis.

caja.title: Holding together what none can hold alone.
caja.body: A resistance fund is a common pot that keeps a struggle going when defending it costs money. It pays for what the mobilisation needs —materials, transport, outreach, logistics— and stays open to support the workforce in whatever disputes the assembly decides. Its first outlay went to the mobilisation; nothing is ruled out for the future. It lowers the personal cost of defending a collective right, so that the decision to take a stand does not depend on anyone's bank balance.

principios.d: Those who can, contribute; those who need it and meet the criteria, receive.
Every euro in and out is recorded and can be inspected.
The fund is run by a committee of the workforce itself, under collective control.
The strength is not in one large gift, but in many small ones sustained over time.

donantes.note: The governance dossier (who runs the fund, how the money is controlled and what happens to whatever is not distributed) will be published once the working groups produce it. It is a different document from the dispute dossier. No banking or tax details will be published unverified, nor will any organisation be shown as a supporter without verifiable confirmation.

items.a: A committee of the workforce itself, under collective control and with traceability of every operation. You can reach it at enfadadosconairbus.contacto@gmail.com and syndicat.util.interempresas@airbus.com.

items.q: What is the money spent on?
items.a: On what the mobilisation needs and the assembly approves: materials, transport, outreach and logistics. Each campaign publishes its expense breakdown — production of each campaign item, travel to the marches, digital infrastructure — on its page, under Campaigns.

items.q: How do I know the money is used well?
items.a: Because every published figure comes from the fund account statements, reconciled by the Treasury, and carries its update date: amount raised, expenses, available balance and number of contributions, with the expense breakdown for each campaign. The downloadable financial report will be published in the coming days.

Yes. No names appear on the site: the wall only counts contributions. Your payment details are seen by Stripe or your bank, and by ÚTIL’s Treasury only to reconcile the accounts and, if you ask, to issue you a receipt.

items.q: Can I contribute from outside Spain?
items.a: Yes. The fund is designed to receive national and international solidarity.
Generally not: a contribution to a resistance fund does not usually count as a deductible donation. Check your particular situation before deducting anything.

items.q: Why is there a section for major donors and institutions?
items.a: Because a large contribution — from another union, an association, a foundation or an individual — usually needs more than a button: documentation on the dispute and on how the fund is governed, a receipt and, sometimes, a conversation with the committee first. That section brings all of this together. Online payments go up to {max}; above that, contributions are made by bank transfer, which arrives in full. No organisation will be shown as a supporter without its confirmation.

items.q: What happens to the fund when the dispute ends?
items.a: It does not close. It pays for what the mobilisation needs and stays open to support the workforce in whatever disputes the assembly decides.

aviso.title: Legal notice
aviso.body:
Site ownership. This website is the resistance fund of the #EnfadadosconAirbus movement. Its legal ownership is held by Sindicato Útil, which is accountable for the fund and signs these legal texts. The movement itself is independent: it does not represent Airbus or use its corporate identity, and it is not the general channel of the holding union or of any other organisation.

Controller. The holding entity is Sindicato Útil (Unión de Trabajadores Independientes y Libres); its identifying details appear at the foot of this notice. The fund receives contributions by bank transfer and by online payment through Stripe (card, Apple Pay, Google Pay, Bizum and other methods).

Purpose. To run the resistance fund: to inform about the fund, channel contributions and, where applicable, the sale of items whose margin goes to the fund (Spanish Law 34/2002 on information society services and e-commerce).

Transparency. The fund's figures are published with their update date and are traceable to real movements; no figure is published without backing.

Intellectual property. This site's own texts may be reproduced with attribution. Third-party trademarks, trade names and distinctive signs that appear belong to their owners and are used for information only, to identify the company the dispute concerns.

Links. The site may link to external sources. It is not responsible for the content or policies of those sites.

Content removal. Anyone who considers that content infringes their rights may request its removal at enfadadosconairbus.contacto@gmail.com, stating the specific content and the reason. It will be handled diligently.

Governing law. This notice is governed by Spanish law.

privacidad.title: Privacy policy
privacidad.body:
This is a translation for information purposes. The Spanish version is the binding one in the event of any discrepancy.

This site is designed to be read without leaving a trace. There is no third-party analytics, no pixels and no advertising profiles.

Data controller. Legal ownership is held by Sindicato Útil (Unión de Trabajadores Independientes y Libres, tax ID G10605053), registered at Paseo John Lennon, s/n, 28906 Getafe, Spain. Contact: enfadadosconairbus.contacto@gmail.com.

What data are processed.
1. None, if you only browse. Your IP address, your browser and the pages you view are not recorded for analytics purposes. The server generates temporary technical logs, standard to any hosting, which are not used to build profiles.
2. Visit counter. A number is incremented. No IP address, identifier, cookie or any data allowing one person to be told from another is stored: there is no processing of personal data.
3. If you write to the contact address. Your email address and the content of your message will be processed for the sole purpose of replying to you. Legal basis: your consent in writing to us. Retention: for as long as the exchange lasts and the legally required period.
4. Contributions by bank transfer. The transfer is made from your bank: this site does not process the payment or see your bank details. Only the data you provide when writing to us —for example to request a receipt— will be processed.
5. Campaign material orders. If you order an item, your name, your email, the chosen pickup point and, if you provide it, your phone number are processed, together with the order details and its payment status, for the sole purpose of managing it, emailing you about the payment and the pickup, and delivering it. Legal basis: performance of that sales contract at your request. Retention: the time needed for delivery and the applicable accounting and tax periods.
6. Online payments (contributions and campaign material orders). They take place on Stripe's payment page (Stripe Payments Europe, Ltd., Ireland), which collects and processes your card or payment-method details under its own privacy policy (stripe.com/privacy). This site neither sees nor stores those details. The holding entity receives from Stripe the amount, the date, the payment method used, your email and, if you provide it, your name, for the sole purpose of recording and reconciling the contribution or order and, if you ask, issuing your receipt. Legal basis: your request to contribute or to buy, and the holding entity's accounting and tax obligations. Retention: the applicable accounting and tax periods.
7. Suggestion box. If you send us a suggestion, we process its text and, only if you provide it, the contact you leave so that we can reply. It reaches the contact address by email and is not stored on the website: your IP address and browser are not recorded. To stop automated spam, opening the suggestion box loads Cloudflare Turnstile, which processes your IP address and technical data about your connection and browser for the sole purpose of telling a person from a program, not to identify or profile anyone. Legal basis: your consent when sending it. Retention: as long as needed to consider it and, if you ask, to reply.

Preferences stored on your device. The browser's local storage is used to remember the chosen language, the display mode (day or night), whether you have already seen the cookie notice and, if you change them, your preferences for the animated striker (shown or hidden, with or without sound). It does not leave your device and is not shared.

Recipients. Data are neither transferred nor sold. The site is hosted and served from Cloudflare, Inc.'s infrastructure, which acts as data processor and also hosts the orders database; it may process technical logs and that data on servers inside and outside the European Economic Area, with the safeguards provided for in the GDPR. Online payments are processed by Stripe Payments Europe, Ltd. (see point 6), which may process data outside the European Economic Area with the safeguards provided for in the GDPR. Order emails are sent through Resend, Inc. (United States), and orders are managed in a Google spreadsheet (Google Ireland Ltd.); both act as data processors, with the safeguards provided for in the GDPR for international transfers.

Your rights. You may request access, rectification, erasure, restriction, objection and portability by writing to enfadadosconairbus.contacto@gmail.com. If you consider that your rights have not been upheld, you may lodge a complaint with the Spanish Data Protection Agency (AEPD, www.aepd.es).

Minors. This site is not directed at children under 14 and does not knowingly collect their data.

cookies.title: Cookie policy
cookies.body:
This is a translation for information purposes. The Spanish version is the binding one in the event of any discrepancy.

This site uses no tracking, advertising or analytics cookies, and browsing it installs no cookie at all, neither our own nor third-party.

Strictly necessary storage. These preferences are stored in your browser, via local storage: the chosen language, the display mode (day or night), whether you have already seen this notice and, only if you change them, whether you prefer to hide the animated striker and whether you have turned its sound on. They identify no one, are not sent to any server and you can delete them from your browser whenever you wish. Given their technical nature they are exempt from the prior consent requirement (article 22.2 of the LSSI-CE).

Third-party services that only activate if you use them. When any page loads, your browser does not contact third-party servers: fonts, images, the animated model and data are served from this same domain. Only in these three cases, and only when you take the action, do external services come in that may use cookies or storage on their own domains:

1. Suggestion box: Cloudflare Turnstile (Cloudflare, Inc.). Opening the suggestion box loads an anti-spam check from challenges.cloudflare.com. It processes your IP address and technical browser data, and may use cookies or local storage on its own domain, solely to tell a person from an automated program; it is not used for advertising or to track you across websites. It installs nothing on this domain. It is a security measure strictly necessary to provide the service you request —sending the suggestion— and is therefore exempt from consent (article 22.2 of the Spanish LSSI-CE). More information: cloudflare.com/turnstile-privacy-policy.

2. Press coverage videos: YouTube (Google Ireland Ltd.). Each video is shown as a still image served from this domain, and YouTube is not loaded until you press “play”; it then runs in privacy-enhanced mode (youtube-nocookie.com). Once you play a video, YouTube may store cookies or data in your browser's storage under its own policy (policies.google.com/technologies/cookies). If you would rather avoid this, do not press “play”.

3. Online contributions: Stripe (Stripe Payments Europe, Ltd.). When you contribute by card or another online payment method, you are taken to Stripe's payment page, outside this domain. There, Stripe uses its own cookies, needed to process the payment securely and prevent fraud (stripe.com/legal/cookies-policy). This site installs no Stripe cookie.

Visit counter. It is our own and merely increments a number on the server. It uses no cookies and stores no data about visitors.

How to revoke. Simply delete the site's local storage from your browser preferences. You will lose no content: you will just be asked for the language again and shown the notice again, and the striker will reappear, muted. Any cookies that YouTube, Cloudflare or Stripe may have stored on their own domains can also be deleted from your browser settings.

condiciones.title: Contribution terms
condiciones.body:
This is a translation for information purposes. The Spanish version is the binding one in the event of any discrepancy.

These terms govern contributions to the resistance fund. The fund receives contributions by bank transfer and by online payment through Stripe. On online payments Stripe deducts its fee (1.25% + €0.25 per payment); by bank transfer, the contribution arrives in full.

What a contribution is. A voluntary transfer of money, without consideration, intended to provide financial support to those who lose wages by joining the action. It is not a purchase, it is not an investment and it creates no right over the fund or its management.

Who may contribute. Any person of legal age with capacity to dispose of the funds they hand over, whether or not they work at Airbus Spain.

Use of funds. Entirely for the purposes of the fund: aid for workers affected by loss of wages and expenses directly necessary to manage it. The distribution criteria will be published together with the constitution of the fund and will not be applied retroactively.

Transparency and accountability. Amounts collected, amounts delivered, management costs and the balance pending allocation will be published periodically, with their update date. No figure will be published without being traceable to a real transaction.

Refunds. Once made, a contribution is irrevocable by its own solidarity-based nature and cannot be refunded.

Receipts and taxation. A receipt will be issued for each contribution. Contributions to a resistance fund do not generally qualify as a tax-deductible donation: check your particular situation before deducting anything.

Campaign materials. Sales of items are not contributions: they are sales contracts, with their own rights of withdrawal and warranty. Each item states what part of the price covers cost and what part goes to the fund. Items are paid for online through Stripe.

Amendments. These terms may be updated. The version applicable to each contribution will be the one in force at the time it is made, and previous versions will remain accessible.

sobre.metaDescription: What the #EnfadadosconAirbus resistance fund is, how it is governed, who is accountable for it, and why it is an independent tool of the workforce.
sobre.title: The fund belongs to the workforce.

naturaleza.heading: Nature
naturaleza.body:
This website is the resistance fund of the #EnfadadosconAirbus movement: a common pot that pays for what the mobilisation needs and that stays open, as a permanent fund, to support the workforce in the disputes and negotiations the assembly decides. Its first outlay financed the mobilisation; the fund is not closed when it ends.

The fund is run by the Strike Committee and Logistics working groups, drawn from the workforce itself, under collective control and public accountability. Its legal and fiscal holder is Sindicato Útil, which provides the tax ID and the bank account and signs the legal texts. The funds are earmarked: they are used exclusively for the purposes agreed by the competent assembly.

This site does not represent Airbus or speak in its name, nor is it the general channel of any trade union: it is the movement's financial tool.

criterio.heading: Governance and control
criterio.intro: The fund's independence is not a statement, it is rules:
items: From the moment it arrives, the money belongs 100% to Sindicato Útil and sits in a separate account in its name; no individual —officer, delegate, member or volunteer— owns it personally, and no private accounts are used.

Every payment requires the joint signature of the Presidency and the Treasury and is backed by an invoice, receipt or supporting document. Anyone with a personal interest in an expense abstains from authorising it.
The Treasury and the assemblies' logistics group jointly keep the record of income and expenses, review the balances periodically and preserve the supporting documents.

The use of the money is decided by the competent assembly —the assembly of striking Airbus España workers— with majority backing of the workforce, counted by individuals and not by union representation. Between disputes, the fund is frozen except for account fees.
criterio.coda: The holding union provides the legal cover; the voice and the control remain with the workforce.

privacidad.heading: Data of those who contribute
privacidad.body: The website collects no data from contributors: there is no sign-up or contributor form, and no list of names is published. If you give by card or Bizum, payment takes place on Stripe's page, which passes on to the fund only what is essential to record the contribution and, if you ask, issue your receipt; if you give by bank transfer, the fund sees what any recipient of a transfer sees. None of this is published.

correcciones.heading: Corrections and contact
correcciones.body:
If you spot an error on the site, a personal detail published by oversight or something misleading, write to enfadadosconairbus.contacto@gmail.com and it will be reviewed.

We are working to give the fund's figures full traceability to real movements and to show it transparently. We will do so as soon as possible; in the meantime, if you spot something that does not add up, tell us.

independencia.heading: Independence
independencia.body:
The fund is independent of the company and of any particular trade union. Sindicato Útil is its legal and fiscal holder; how the funds are used is decided by the competent assembly. The #EnfadadosconAirbus movement belongs to the workforce and aims to remain its voice in potential future disputes and negotiations.

Third-party trademarks and names that appear are used only to identify the actors in the dispute, with no intent to create confusion about the origin of this site.

reglamentoReparto.heading: Allocation rules
reglamentoReparto.body:
These rules set out what the fund's money is used for. The competent assembly approves them and only it can amend them.

The money goes to expenses directly related to the mobilisation: production of campaign material and posters (including the T-shirts), transport and travel to the marches, hire of equipment —such as the truck with a PA system for the march on the Ministries on 12 September 2026—, communication and outreach, professional services and logistics, and the account's fees and upkeep. Personal expenses or any unrelated to union activity may not be charged.

Every expense is accounted for before the assembly and published with its date, traceable to real transactions and backed by its supporting document. When a different organisation fronts an expense of the mobilisation, the competent assembly approves it before it is charged to the fund.

At the end of each mobilisation the fund is neither closed nor is the surplus shared out: the remainder stays in the fund, available for future mobilisations of the Airbus España workforce linked to labour disputes and their collective bargaining. Sindicato Útil cannot use that remainder without the authorisation of the competent assembly; between disputes the money is frozen, and only the competent assembly may decide to close the fund and the final destination of the remainder.

The full texts of the agreement that created the fund and of these rules will be published here in the coming days.

campanas.title: One fund, many fights.
campanas.intro: The fund was not opened for a single dispute and does not close when one ends. Each campaign is a fight it has carried, with what it cost and what it paid for. Whatever is left over passes to the next one.

huelga-2026.lema: Win back lost purchasing power, and have decisions negotiated rather than imposed.
huelga-2026.conseguido:
Before the strike, what the company put on the table was more of the same: years of cuts to working conditions. The CEO's plan to cut remote work to 20% a week was the spark for a historic mobilisation. This is what was on the table then, and what is in the agreement the workforce approved in a referendum on 1 October, with 76.76% of the votes and a turnout of 87.33%.

Along the way, the workforce voted down July's provisional deal in a referendum —a 12% that was really a 10% general rise plus two points going to RSI and promotions— and held the strike when asked whether to pause it: on 31 August, 81.2% voted to carry on. And when the company took its "final proposal" to the Ministry of Industry instead of to the assemblies and called the referendum on its own, the National Court suspended it at CGT's request. The interim measures were lifted on 24 September; the substance —whether the right to strike was violated— is heard on 4 November.

The fund has paid for what it took to get here: the T-shirts, the trains to the Seville and Madrid marches, the transport to the Ministry.

filas.antes: A 3% general rise, plus 0.5% for RSI and 0.5% for promotions, in 2026 and 2027.
filas.despues: A four-year agreement with real CPI guaranteed and recovery of 7.95% of purchasing power: real CPI + 2% in 2026, 2027 and 2028, and real CPI + 1.95% in 2029. On top of that, every year, 0.5% for individual pay reviews and 0.5% for promotions.
Pushed back to 2028, and a one-off gross payment of €2,000 (non-consolidated), in October 2026, compensates it for everyone on the payroll when the referendum is validated.

filas.antes: Cut to 20% a week from 1 September 2026: the spark for the strike.
filas.despues: The current policy stays and individual agreements are respected, including 40% remote and two days a week from home. This also applies to new hires.

filas.antes: The Bradford factor to measure absenteeism.
filas.despues: The company withdraws its appeal to the Supreme Court, drops the removal of the sick-leave supplement altogether and repays what was deducted in October. A new absenteeism control system will be negotiated in a joint working group.
Current routes are kept. Any changes, including August's, are negotiated in the Mobility Committees.
Two compulsory weeks and two flexible ones (previously three and one), scheduled between employee and supervisor.

filas.antes: No guarantees for the staff affected.
filas.despues: Anyone moving to the joint venture keeps the Collective Agreement from day one until a new one exists, their seniority and full access to Airbus's internal job market, with no probation period.
Before 1 November 2026, a committee will review current agreements and future activity needs.

comparativa.ademasTitulo: And what wasn't even on the table
ademas: Canteen: for those without free access, the price drops from €5 to €3.50 from 1 October, with an annual price review.
Voluntary flexible start and finish times in the roles that allow it.

Pay policy: a full review of PG-121 to improve progression and promotions; of conditions for LMA, rodadores and ENDS; a new job catalogue and a new variable pay system (PG-22). Negotiations start before the end of 2026.

elecciones-2027.lema: Let the workforce choose who represents it, with the means to campaign.

meta.title: Guide to the proposal · Referendum
meta.description: A point-by-point guide to the «proposed agreement» that the Airbus Spain workforce votes on: what it offers, what is left to specify and why it matters.

hero.intro: The «proposed agreement» put to a referendum sets out pay, remote work, absence, canteen and more. This guide goes through it point by point: what it offers, what is left to specify and why it matters, so you can decide with all the information.

estado.texto: The referendum took place on 30 September and 1 October, online and in person, with observers from every participating union and the external consultancy PwC. With a turnout of 87.33%, the workforce approved the agreement: 76.76% of the votes cast were 'yes', 20.26% 'no' and 2.98% abstentions. The substance of CGT's claim is heard on 4 November.

cuerpo: A proposal can sound good and, at the same time, leave for later the details that decide how it works in practice.
Asking for the improvements to be written down, quantified and guaranteed before voting is not rejecting them: it is making sure they are delivered.

guia.intro: Filter by topic and open each point to see what the proposal offers, what is left to specify and why it matters.

puntos.pregunta: What is locked in, and until when?
puntos.propuesta: The company presents the agreement as binding in all its terms; any change in the 2028 collective agreement would require a new agreement between the parties.
puntos.falta: What is voted on is a «framework», not the final wording of the collective agreement, which is drafted afterwards. And the company warns that, if it is rejected, there will be no further negotiation until 2028: a «this or nothing» that conditions the vote, and whose good faith in bargaining is precisely what the Audiencia Nacional examines on 4 November.
puntos.importa: An agreement can be binding and still leave the detail to a later text; and presenting the vote as having no alternative puts pressure on the decision.
puntos.clave: Binding should not mean voting under the pressure of «this or nothing».

puntos.pregunta: Which document is published, and negotiated with whom?
puntos.propuesta: If the referendum passes, the Ministry of Labour will publish the framework in the BOE «in full», with no changes.
puntos.falta: The framework «will serve as the basis» for the final agreement that amends the collective agreement's articles; that final text is drafted later, and it is not specified which union side would sign it.
puntos.importa: The legal value depends on the final collective-agreement text and on who signs it, not just on the framework being voted.
puntos.clave: Publishing in the BOE does not yet say which articles are signed, or with whom.

puntos.pregunta: How is it calculated, and what happens with the deviation?
puntos.propuesta: The initial CPI is the Bank of Spain's projection (February); with the INE's final figure (December) the deviation is settled and adjusted in the following year's General Increase. Arrears are paid in a single payment in January or February 2027.
puntos.falta: There are no caps or floors: an over-projection is deducted from the next year's increase. And in the company's own example it is not clear whether the differential (the «delta») is consolidated into the annual base or paid only as a one-off arrear.
puntos.importa: Without a floor, a low-CPI year relies only on the fixed percentage; and whether the delta consolidates or not changes what is paid in later years.
puntos.clave: What matters is not only the CPI, but whether its correction adds to the base or stays a one-off payment.

puntos.pregunta: Where does it come from, and who does it reach?
puntos.propuesta: The 7.95% is spread over four years (2026 +2%, 2027 +2%, 2028 +2%, 2029 +1.95%, on real CPI), plus 0.5% RSI and 0.5% promotions each year. It starts from the 7.6% of 2020–2025 CPI minus the general increases paid, raised to 7.95%.
puntos.falta: The calculation compares only against general increases and excludes individual raises, so it does not measure each person's real loss; and the 0.5% RSI and 0.5% promotions are selective: they do not reach the whole workforce equally.
puntos.importa: A headline 7.95% is not the same as what each payslip recovers.
puntos.clave: The total matters less than how it is split and who it reaches.

puntos.pregunta: What is guaranteed about variable pay?
puntos.propuesta: The proposal guarantees that the variable-pay percentages will not be reduced (V.1 12%, V.2 10%, VI 8%, VIII 6%) and proposes negotiating a new system, with a review of the salary policy (PG-121D) before the end of 2026.
puntos.falta: The percentage is locked in, but not how it is earned: the new system («to simplify the model») is still to be negotiated, and that is where what is actually paid is decided.
puntos.importa: Keeping the percentage does not guarantee the criteria that decide whether it is reached.
puntos.clave: The how-much is protected; the how is not.

puntos.pregunta: A commitment to a result, or to negotiate?
puntos.propuesta: There is a commitment to negotiate a new job catalogue and to review PG-121D and the terms for LMA, rodadores and ENDs, with talks starting before the end of 2026.
puntos.falta: It is a commitment to negotiate and analyse, with a start date but no guaranteed result or closing deadline.
puntos.importa: Starting to negotiate in 2026 does not ensure what is agreed, or when.
puntos.clave: There is a start date, not a finish.

puntos.propuesta: A 40% effective remote-work rate applies to the current workforce and new hires; justified absences do not count towards that 40%, the 2-day agreements are respected and a half-day option is added.
puntos.falta: Respecting the existing agreements keeps their unilateral-withdrawal clause: either party can cancel remote work, with no justification and one month's notice. The 40% is not shielded from that clause, and the monthly or quarterly distribution depends on the manager.
puntos.importa: A 40% that can be withdrawn unilaterally with one month's notice is not a guaranteed minimum.
puntos.clave: Without removing the unilateral withdrawal, the 40% is reversible.

puntos.pregunta: What happens when there is no agreement?
puntos.propuesta: Two obligatory weeks and two flexible weeks are kept; the calendar is agreed with each site's works council, and the scheduling between the person and their supervisor, weighing business and personal circumstances «equally».
puntos.falta: «Weighing equally» does not say who decides when the person and the supervisor do not agree on the dates.
puntos.importa: The tie-break is exactly where real work-life balance is decided.
puntos.clave: The rule for when there is no agreement is missing.

puntos.propuesta: The company has withdrawn its appeal before the Supreme Court, fully reverses the withdrawal of the sick-leave top-up and refunds the amounts in October; the new system would be co-designed with the workers' representatives, with criteria agreed transparently.
puntos.falta: The immediate harm is undone, but the new rulebook does not yet exist: what is approved is the commitment to co-design it, not its criteria.
puntos.importa: The guarantee is procedural (joint and transparent), not an already-written system.
puntos.clave: The old harm is reversed; the new system is yet to be written.

puntos.pregunta: And when the new agreement arrives?
puntos.propuesta: Those moving to the Joint Venture keep the local agreement's terms from day one and until a new agreement exists, with internal mobility within Airbus, seniority, no probation, and transport and canteen.
puntos.falta: The protection lasts «until a new agreement exists», whose content is future and unknown.
puntos.importa: A guarantee that ends when the next agreement arrives needs to know what that agreement will bring.
puntos.clave: Protected until the new agreement; what it will say is still unknown.

puntos.pregunta: What is locked in about the price?
puntos.propuesta: For those without free access, the price drops from €5 to €3.5 from early October, with an annual review «keeping the most advantageous conditions»; those who already eat free keep it.
puntos.falta: The guarantee is qualitative («most advantageous conditions»), with no numeric cap to stop the annual review from eroding the improvement.
puntos.importa: With no written cap, an annual review can dilute the €3.5 over time.
puntos.clave: A promise of «the most advantageous» is not a price with a cap.

puntos.pregunta: What level of service is kept?
puntos.propuesta: The current routes are kept and no reduction or removal is foreseen; adjustments would be made by the Mobility Committees.
puntos.falta: The routes are kept, but the level (frequencies, stops, August) is subject to adjustment in committee.
puntos.importa: Keeping the routes is not the same as keeping the level of service.
puntos.clave: Routes guaranteed; frequencies, up for review.

puntos.propuesta: The posts objectively compatible with voluntary flexible start and end times would be identified, according to organisational, productive and safety criteria; production is excluded.
puntos.falta: The criteria are named, but the list of eligible posts is identified later by the company; there is no closed list.
puntos.importa: That the criteria are objective does not yet say which posts benefit.
puntos.clave: Criteria yes; list of posts, pending.

puntos.pregunta: What will it be able to decide?
puntos.propuesta: A specific joint committee (signatory parties and management) is created to analyse, before 1 November 2026, the current agreements and future workload needs in Cádiz.
puntos.falta: It has a date and a joint composition, but its remit is to «analyse»: whether it can decide, and with what effect, is not set.
puntos.importa: A committee that only analyses can end up unable to resolve anything.
puntos.clave: Joint and dated; the power to decide is missing.

antesDeVotar.titulo: There are also questions about the vote itself

items.q: How is the online vote safeguarded?
items.a: The referendum is held online and in person, with union observers and the consultancy PwC. With remote voting, it should be explained how the secrecy, identity and verification of each vote are ensured.

items.q: And custody over the two days?
items.a: As the vote runs over two days, it is still worth explaining how ballot boxes and systems are kept overnight, before the observers of all parties.
A two-day vote needs a clear reason and a transparent procedure that is the same for every site.

cierre.cuerpo: If the proposal can be improved, asking for precision before approving it is a reasonable position. Share this guide so everyone can review the points and decide with all the information.

referendum.nota: Informational guide by the movement. The amounts and conditions come from the public documentation of the proposal; where detail is missing, it is raised as a question.
